title: Cross-boundary Failover Conductor with Telemetry-Gated Standby Certification
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need an automated controller ("Conductor") that can coordinate cross-region failover while guaranteeing that standby fleets meet an empirically derived readiness score before receiving customer traffic. Current warm-standby checks are binary (healthy/unhealthy) and rely on ad-hoc probes; they don't account for cache warmth, model variant compatibility, or recent telemetry trends, which leads to flaky cutovers and user-facing latency spikes.

Goal: Build a Conductor service that aggregates short- and medium-window telemetry, computes a composite readiness score (latency p95, KV cache hit ratio, model-variant compatibility, GPU queue depth, recent error-rate trends), and gates region/tier cutovers and model-variant fallbacks behind a configurable certification policy. The Conductor will: 1) expose an API for rollout orchestration; 2) provide per-region readiness signals usable by routing layers; 3) automatically trigger prefill/poke actions (KV prefetch, synthetic warmups) when readiness is below threshold; 4) enforce safety windows and ramp rules for traffic movement; 5) log decisions to the audit trail for post-mortem.

Non-goals: This ticket will not replace global routing policy config syntax or implement full RBAC for enterprise customers; those are separate follow-ups. Also we will not initially support on-prem private clusters — focus is hosted and dedicated fleets across cloud regions.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor service deployed to staging and integrated with existing region controller
Readiness score computed from at least 5 telemetry signals and accessible via HTTP API
Automated prefill actions (KV prefetch + 10 synthetic requests per model-variant) can be triggered and their effect visible in telemetry within 3 minutes
Policy-gated cutover: attempted traffic shift is blocked when readiness < policy threshold, and allowed when >= threshold
Canary ramp: staged traffic transfer (0 -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on safety violation
Runbook entry and dashboard showing readiness score, contributing signals, and audit log present before rolling to prod
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged Conductor in staging; integrate with test routing layer. 2) Run 72-hour soak with synthetic traffic across two regions and multiple model variants. 3) Gradual deploy to a single low-traffic production tenant behind feature flag; monitor for 48h. 4) Expand to cross-region small-percentage cutovers for non-critical traffic for 7 days. 5) Enable full cutovers for approved tenants. 6) Post-rollout retrospective and adjustments to policy thresholds.
telemetry_requirements: Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per model-variant and region
KV cache hit ratio and KV insertion rate
GPU utilization and queue depth per instance pool
Recent deployment churn and number of in-flight model version swaps
Synthetic warmup success rate and response fidelity
tests: Unit tests for readiness-scoring algorithm (threshold edge cases)
Integration test: Conductor orchestrates synthetic warmups and readiness moves from 0.45 -> 0.85 within 5 minutes
Chaos test: simulate 30% instance eviction during cutover and assert Conductor blocks the cutover
Load test: measured p95 during prefill under typical traffic mix stays within 1.2x baseline
open_questions: What is the correct decay window for telemetry signals (30s vs 5m vs 15m)?
Should model-variant compatibility be weighted higher than cache-warmth for low-latency SLOs?
Do we allow manual override for enterprise tenants with explicit approval? (security/approval workflow needed)
How to represent readiness for heterogeneous fleets (mixed GPU types and quantization levels)?
notes: Decision: initial readiness score will be a weighted sum with configurable weights per project. We will ship with conservative defaults used in the production emergency drills.
Trade-off: stricter gating reduces failover speed but prevents user-impacting latency spikes; policy will be tunable per-customer tier.
Implementation approach: lightweight Conductor in Go, gRPC/mTLS to telemetry aggregator, expose REST for routing layer. Use existing autoscaler hooks to trigger prefill jobs.
